articles.title: उजाड पाखामा चिया खेती, गाउँमै रोजगारी
articles.summary:
दोलखा । दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–४ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँमै रोजगारी सिर्जना गरेको छ । बाँझो जमिन हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र युवाले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गर्दै स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधिमा उल्लेख्य टेवा पु¥याएका छन् ।

दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–९ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँको स्वरूप फेरिएको छ । रोजगारीको अभावका कारण हुने युवा पलायन र बाँदर आतंकजस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्दै चिया खेती स्थानीयका लागि आयआर्जनको भरपर्दो माध्यम बनेको छ ।

पहिले उत्तिसको घारीले ढाकिएको र झुसुले किराको समस्याले विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीसमेत प्रभावित थिए । तर यो क्षेत्र वडा कार्यालयको पहलमा सफा गरी इलामबाट ल्याइएका २५ हजार चियाका बिरुवासहित हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण गरिएको छ ।

प्रारम्भिक परीक्षण सफल भएपछि यसको व्यवस्थापनको जिम्मा स्थानीयको सहभागितामा बनेको सुन्द्रावती चिया विकास समूहलाई हस्तान्तरण गरिएको छ । ७–८ वर्षको अन्तरालमा यहाँ उत्पादित चियाले बजार पाउन थालेको छ ।

प्रति किलो १०० रुपैयाँका दरले चियाको मुना टिप्ने व्यवस्था भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र परीक्षा दिएर बसेका विद्यार्थीले गाउँमै रोजगारी पाएका छन् । बिहानदेखि साँझसम्म काम गर्ने मजदुरले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरिरहेका छन् ।

वडा कार्यालयको बजेट र लगानीमा अघि बढाइएको यस योजनामा चालु आर्थिक वर्ष मात्रै ४ लाख रुपैयाँ थप लगानी गरिएको छ । चिया प्रशोधन सहज बनाउन ६ लाख रुपैयाँ लागतमा तीन प्रकारका आधुनिक प्रशोधन मेसिनसमेत सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ ।

स्थानीय सरकारको सही योजना र निरन्तर लगानी भए बाँझो जमिनलाई पनि आम्दानीको स्रोत बनाउन सकिने उदाहरण सुन्द्रावतीको चिया खेतीले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ ।

articles.title: मारुती सिमेन्टद्वारा जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टलाई CPR तालिमका लागि म्यानिकिन हस्तान्तरण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । हालको परिवेशमा विशेषगरी युवापुस्तामा अस्वस्थ जीवनशैली, अत्यधिक तनाव तथा हृदयसम्बन्धी आकस्मिक समस्याका घटनामा वृद्धि हुँदै गएको अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) तालिमको आवश्यकता बढ्दै गएको छ।

यही आवश्यकतालाई महसुस गर्दै मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेड ले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत देशभर CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने उद्देश्यका साथ जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्ट लाई आवश्यक CPR Training Manikin हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ।

उक्त सामग्री हस्तान्तरण कार्यक्रम दुवै संस्थाका सञ्चालक तथा पदाधिकारीहरूको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको हो। कार्यक्रममा मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेडले समाजप्रतिको आफ्नो उत्तरदायित्व निर्वाह गर्ने प्रतिबद्धतालाई व्यवहारमा उतार्दै स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन पाउँदा खुशी लागेको जनाएको छ।

जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टले प्राप्त CPR Training Manikin को प्रयोग गरी देशभर निःशुल्क वा पहुँचयोग्य CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने, आकस्मिक हृदयाघात वा अन्य आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा सर्वसाधारणले समयमै प्राथमिक उपचार प्रदान गर्न सक्ने जनशक्ति तयार गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेको जनाएको छ।

ट्रस्टका अनुसार CPR सम्बन्धी ज्ञान र सीपको विस्तारले आकस्मिक अवस्थामा बहुमूल्य जीवन बचाउन महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुग्ने विश्वास गरिएको छ। यस सहकार्यले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना बढाउनुका साथै जीवनरक्षा सम्बन्धी सीप विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: सैनिक कल्याणकारी भवन ठेक्का प्रकरण : निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि चरम अन्याय र अर्बौँको लगानी जोखिममा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन भाडामा लिई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ लगानी गरेको श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. चरम प्रशासनिक थिचोमिचो र अन्यायमा परेको निश्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।

भवन हस्तान्तरणमा सेनाकै तर्फबाट भएको ढिलाइ, काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकासँगको नक्सा पास विवाद र कोभिड–१९ को महामारीका कारण उत्पन्न विषम परिस्थितिलाई नजरअन्दाज गर्दै कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले उल्टै निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि एकतर्फी रूपमा करोडौँ बक्यौताको भार थोपरेको पाइएको हो । यस विषयमा अहिले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा मुद्धा पुगेको छ । साथै यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार आयोगमा पनि उजुरी परेको छ ।

प्राप्त दस्तावेज तथा पत्राचारका अनुसार सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोष र श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. बीच २०७६ माघ १६ गते महाँकालस्थानस्थित ‘कल्याणकारी भवन’१५ वर्षका लागि भाडामा लिने सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौताको मुख्य सर्त नै भवन विधिवत रूपमा पूर्ण निर्माण भई हस्तान्तरण भएपछि मात्र भाडा लागू हुने भन्ने थियो । तर, बोलपत्र जारी गर्दाकै बखत उक्त भवनको नक्सा पास नभएको र मापदण्ड विपरीत बढी निर्माण गरिएको भन्दै काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाले काम रोकेपछि सम्झौताको प्रारम्भिक चरणमै विवाद उत्पन्न भएको थियो । सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयको आफ्नै आन्तरिक र कानुनी त्रुटिका कारण समयमा भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेको बताइन्छ ।

पुरक सम्झौताको उल्लंघन र कोभिडको मार

भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेपछि दुवै पक्षबीच वि.सं. २०७८ मङ्सिर २८ गते पुरक सम्झौता गरियो, जसमा भवन हस्तान्तरणको मिति २०७८ असार १ कायम गर्ने प्रयास गरियो । तर, सो अवधिमा देशव्यापी रूपमा फैलिएको कोभिड–१९ को दोस्रो लहर र लकडाउनका कारण भवन पूर्ण रूपमा तयार भई व्यापारिक प्रयोजनका लागि हस्तान्तरण हुनै सकेन ।

व्यापार व्यवसाय ठप्प भएको र बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट कर्जा प्रवाह नभएको यस्तो गम्भीर आर्थिक मन्दीको समयमा नेपाल सरकार रक्षा मन्त्रालयले समेत भाडामा छुट दिन निर्देशन जारी गरेको थियो । सैनिक कोषको आफ्नै कार्यदलले भाडामा ५० प्रतिशत छुट दिने राय पेस गरेपनि निर्देशनालयका केही अधिकारीहरूको बदनियतका कारण व्यवसायीले पाउनुपर्ने उक्त कानुनी छुट रकम उपलब्ध गराइएन ।

प्रशासनको उल्झन

निर्माण कम्पनीका एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरका अनुसार, खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहेको भवनलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ निजी लगानी गरेर मासिक ५ करोड ६३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी भाडा उठ्ने सुनिश्चित व्यावसायिक केन्द्र बनाएपछि सैनिक कोषका केही अधिकारीहरूको ‘गिद्धे नजर’ यसमा परेको हो ।

कम्पनीले पटक–पटक पारदर्शी हिसाब मिलानका लागि लिखित अनुरोध गर्दा समेत त्यसलाई बेवास्ता गर्दै उल्टै पानी र बिजुलीको लाइन काट्ने, लिफ्ट प्रयोग गर्न नदिने र कम्पनीका कर्मचारीहरूमाथि कार्यस्थलमै भौतिक आक्रमण गर्नेसम्मका निकृष्ट कार्यहरू भएका छन् । जसले गर्दा व्यवसायी मानसिक र आर्थिक रूपमा पूर्णतः धराशयी हुने अवस्थामा पुगेका छन् ।

निष्पक्ष छानबिन र हिसाब फरफारकको माग

नेपाली सेनासँग लामो समयदेखि विकट भूगोल र ब्यारेकहरूमा समेत निर्माण कार्य गरी व्यावसायिक सम्बन्ध कायम राखेको यस कम्पनीले रक्षा मन्त्रालय, प्रधानसेनापति कार्यालय र बालाध्यक्ष विभागमा बोधार्थ दिँदै एक उच्चस्तरीय निष्पक्ष छानबिन टोली गठन गर्न माग गरेको छ । कम्पनीले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषलाई कुनै रकम तिर्नु बुझाउनु पर्ने बाँकी नरहेको, उल्टै कल्याणकारी कोषको तर्फबाट भएको सम्झौता उल्लंघन र अनाधिकृत रकम असुलीका कारण आफूले अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ क्षतिपूर्ति पाउनुपर्ने दाबी गरेको छ । राज्यको शक्तिशाली अंगको आडमा एउटा वैधानिक निर्माण व्यवसायीको निजी सम्पत्ति र लगानीमाथि गरिएको यो चरम दोहनले नेपालमा निजी क्षेत्रको लगानी कति असुरक्षित छ भन्ने गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ ।

भवन ठेक्कामा करिब २० करोड हिनामिना आरोप

काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन ठेक्का प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयका उच्च अधिकारी र कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा झण्डै २० करोड रुपैयाँ बराबरको ठूलो आर्थिक हिनामिना भएको गम्भीर आरोप लागेको छ । श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा। लि। का एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषका तत्कालीन उच्च अधिकारी र हालका प्रमुख अवकाशप्राप्त जर्नेल सुनिल राज विष्ट,कर्मचारीहरू नानिराम थापा र कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायतले शक्तिको दुरुपयोग गरी अर्बौँको निजी लगानी डुबाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिबाट भवन व्यवस्थापन कार्यालयमा पदस्थापन भएका नानिराम थापा,कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायत त्यहाँ कार्यरत कर्मचारीहरुको मिलेमतोमा उक्त भवनमा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले उठाउनुपर्ने भाडा बिजुली महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज असुल गरेको आरोप लागेको हो ।

त्यस्तै,यो टोलीले निर्माण व्यवसायी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरसँग मात्र होइन,त्यस भवनमा व्यवसाय गरिरहेका विभिन्न व्यापारीलाई नाम सारी तथा राम्रो लोकेशनको पसल उपलब्ध गराइदिने प्रलोभनमा पारी रकम उठाइरहेको बुढाको गम्भीर आरोप छ ।

त्यसैगरी बुढाका अनुसार यी पात्रहरुले अदालतलाई समेत विभिन्न माध्यमबाट दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने र मुद्दालाई कम्जोर बनाएर आफ्नो काला कर्तुतहरु लुकाउन खोजेको उनले बताएका छन् ।

कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले बोलपत्र आह्वान गर्दा भवनको नक्सा पास नै नभएको र महानगरको अवरोधका कारण निर्माण कम्पनीले समयमा काम सुरु गर्न नपाएको, भवन पूर्ण रूपमा निर्माण नै नभई र खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहँदा समेत निर्देशनालयले पुरै अवधिको पूर्ण भाडा दाबी गरी पत्र पठाउनु कानुनी रूपमा त्रुटिपूर्ण रहेको, कम्पनीले आफ्नै खर्चमा जडान गरेको ट्रान्सफर्मर, विद्युतीकरण, खानेपानी प्रणाली, र लिफ्ट जस्ता पूर्वाधारहरू कल्याणकारी भवन व्यवस्थापनले एकतर्फी रूपमा नियन्त्रणमा लिई व्यवसायीलाई प्रवेशमा रोक लगाएको आरोप लागेको छ ।

भवन व्यवस्थापनकै केही कर्मचारीहरूले व्यापारीहरूबाट सोझै करिब १ करोड ३५ लाख विद्युत महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज उठाएको साथै २०७९ साल श्रावण,भदौ र असोज ५ गतेसम्मको पुरै भवन भाडा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिको बैंक ग्यारेन्टीबाट असुल गरेको र त्यहाँ व्यवसायी गरिरहेका ब्यापारीहरुबाट समेत असुल गरी सो रकम हिसाबमा मिलान नगरी गायब पारेको अर्को गम्भिर आरोप पनि छ ।

कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको मिटर तथा बिलिङ सफ्टवेयर नक्कली हस्ताक्षर प्रयोग गरी अनाधिकृत रूपमा नामसारी गरिएको र कम्पनीले अर्बौँ खर्चेर बनाएका संरचनाहरू सहमति बिना भत्काएर दोहन गरिएको आरोप छ ।

त्यस्तै,अहिले यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार लगायतका स्वतन्त्र निकायहरुले वास्तविक छानबिन गरिरहेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतमा समेत मुद्दा चलिरहेको निर्माण व्यवसायी बुढा मगरले जानकारी दिए । उनका अनुसार सर्वोच्च अदालतले १५ श्रावणमा दुबैपक्षलाई छलफलका लागि बोलाएको हुँदा उक्त छलफलबाट सकारात्मक नतिजा आउने बुढा मगरले विश्वास गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: एनसेल अब सरकारको नाममा आउने, सर्वोच्चको बोल्ड फैसलापछि वालेन्द्रको परीक्षा शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । एनसेल निजी क्षेत्रको अग्रणी सञ्चार माध्यमको रुपमा स्थापित कम्पनी हो। तर, एनसेलले नेपालमा गरिरहेको व्यापार र सेवा प्रवाह भने विवादास्पद नै छ। कर प्रकरणदेखि अन्य विषयमा समेत लम्बेतान विवादमा फसेको एनसेलको सेयर किनबेचपछि भने यसबारेका प्रश्नको सवालमा सर्वोच्च अदालतको आदेशपछि थप कानूनी प्रष्टतासहित अवैध गतिविधिविरुद्ध नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको कार्यान्वयन गर्न सक्षम छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ ।

लामो समय कर विवादमा फसेको एनसेल नेपालको अग्रणी निजी क्षेत्रको टेलिकम सेवा प्रदायक बन्न पुग्यो। नेपालको टेलिकम क्षेत्रमा नविनताका निम्ति काम गरेको एनसेलले सञ्चारको क्षेत्रमा खेलेको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न गर्ने ठाउँ छैन्।

अझं भन्नुपर्दा सरकारी स्वामित्वको नेपाल टेलिकमले दिने सेवालाई एनसेलले दिएको चुनौतीकै कारण सञ्चार क्षेत्रले नेपालमा राम्रो स्तरको सेवा प्रवाहमा काम गरेको पाइन्छ। तर, एनसेलको यो राम्रो पाटोसंगै विवाद भने अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण छन्। हरेक वर्ष मनग्य आम्दानी पनि दिएको एनसेलले विदेशमा नोपलबाट ठूलो धनराशी पठाएको छ।

सेवासंगै मेवा पनि दिएको एनसेलले केहि विवाद यस्ता पनि भोग्यो, जुन नेपालको कानूनको प्रत्यक्ष उल्लङ्घन र राज्यविरुद्ध गरेको एकखाले अपराध नै हो। कर छली विवाद लामो समयसम्म लम्बिदा एनसेलले आफ्ना भौतिक संरचनामा क्षति व्यहोर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। अझं, तत्कालीन विप्लव नेतृत्वको नेकपाले एनसेलको कार्यालयमा बम विस्फोट गराएपछि सेक्युरिटी गार्डले ज्यान नै दिने स्थिति बन्यो। यसरी देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रका भौतिक संरचनामा किन आक्रमण भए? यसका पछाडी कारण हुन्, एनसेलले नेपालको कानून पालना गर्न भन्दा बढि मुनाफा आर्जन गर्ने ध्येय राख्नु।

सेयर खरिदबिक्रीको घोटाला

एनसेलले गरेको सेयर खरिदबिक्री भने अस्वभाविकमात्रै थिएन, सार्वभौम मुलुकको स्वाधिनतामाथिको प्रहार नै थियो। नेपालले निर्माण गरेको कानून व्यवसायमैत्री थिएन भनेपनि त्यो कानून नेपालको सार्वभौमसत्तासंग जोडिएको विषय थियो।

नेपालको संसदले निर्माण गरेको कानून नेपालभित्र सबैलाई मान्य र बाध्यकारी हुन्छ। तर, एनसेलको हकमा यो लागू नहुने गरि गरिएको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीमा सर्वोच्चको झड्कापछि भने नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको पालना निर्वाध गराउनसक्छ भन्ने प्रष्ट सन्देश दिएको छ ।

सेयर खरिदबिक्री अमान्य

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशद्वय सपना प्रधान मल्ल र टेकप्रसाद ढुंगानाको संयुक्त इजलासले विवादास्पद सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भन्दै खारेज गरिदिएको छ।

यसले एनसेलको अध्यक्ष बन्न पुगेका सतिसलाल आचार्य अब कर्मचारीको हैसियतमा पुगेका छन भने एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व रेनोल्ड होल्डिङ्स लिमिटेडको वास्तविक मालिक मलेसियन कम्पनी आजियाटाकै रहेको ठहर गरेको छ। सतिसलालको कम्पनी स्पेक्ट्रलाइट युकेले किनेको भनिएको ८० प्रतिशत सेयर अमान्य भएको छ ।

के भन्यो सर्वोच्चले ?

सर्वोच्च अदालतले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व ६ अर्ब हाराहारीमा भएको कारोबारलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भनेको छ । अदालतले सन् २०१६ मा करिब १ खर्ब ४३ अर्ब रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरिएको शेयरलाई अत्यन्तै न्यून मूल्यमा किनबेच गरिएको भन्नुलाई नै कानूनको उल्लङ्घनको रुपमा ठहर गरेको हो। सर्वोच्चले आदेशमा भनेको छ, ’शेयर खरीद बिक्री कारोबारको बारेमा विदेशी लगानी तथा प्रविधि हस्तान्तरण ऐन, २०७५ को दफा १९ को अभिलेख राख्ने व्यवस्थासँग आफूलाई अनुमति दिने, नियमन गर्ने विशेष कानूनको रूपमा रहेको दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (१) (ट) को व्यवस्थालाई नजरअन्दाज गर्न मिल्ने देखिएन ।

प्रस्तुत संशोधित ऐ. नियम १५ ( १ ) (ट) तथा नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण ( अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ को विनियम (१), (३) र विनियम ४ को खण्ड (क) लाई चुनौति दिएको अवस्था पनि रहेको छैन । अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्ति विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको ८०% शेयर धारण गर्ने शेयरवाला आजियाटा इन्भेष्टमेन् (यु.के.) लिमिटेडले आफ्नो शेयर स्पेक्ट्रलाइट यु.के. लिमिटेडलाई मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार १ डिसेम्बर २०२३) मा बिक्री गरेको तथ्यमा विवाद देखिदैन । उक्त शेयर कारोवार हुनु अगावै नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट पूर्व स्वीकृति लिनुपर्नेमा नलिएको, विपक्षीबाट पेस भएको लिखित जवाफमा शेयरधनीको शेयर खरीद बिक्री हुँदा प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था नै छैन भन्ने जिकिर लिएको र मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार डिसेम्वर १ सन् २०२३) मा भएको शेयर खरीद बिक्री सम्झौताको सम्बन्धमा मिति २०८०।११।१२ मा मात्र स्वीकृतिको लागि प्राधिकरणमा निवेदन पेस गरेको स्थिति देखिएकाले विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले दुर सञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ र नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण (अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ र अनुमतिपत्रको शर्तसमेत अक्षरशः परिपालना गर्दै पारदर्शी र विधिसम्मत तरिकाले सेवा संचालन गर्नू भनी विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको नाममा निर्देशनात्मक आदेश जारी गरिदिएको छ ।’

यसरी हेर्दा अब एनसेलको सञ्चालन एनसेल आजियाटाले नै गर्नुपर्नेछ। यसरी हेर्दा सतिसलालले गरेको कारोबार अवैध ठहर भएको छ भने अब ससितलाल एनसेलको अध्यक्षभन्दा पनि कर्मचारी वा अन्य हैसियतमा पुग्ने भएका छन्।

अब सरकारीकरणको बाटो खुला

नेपालको दूरसञ्चार ऐनले निश्वित अवधिपछि निश्चित कानूनी बाटो पुरा नगरेमा टेलिकम कम्पनी नेपाल सरकारको नाममा स्वतः आउने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। जसअनुसार दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ३३ अनुसार ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी विदेशी लगानी भएका दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीहरूको अनुमतिपत्रको २५ वर्षे अवधि समाप्त भएपछि त्यसको स्वामित्व स्वतः नेपाल सरकारमा हस्तान्तरण हुने व्यवस्था गरेको छ ।

एनसेलले १६ भदौ २०६१ मा अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरेकाले १५ भदौ २०८६ मा यसको २५ वर्षे अवधि पुरा हुनेछ । जुन अवधिपछि एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्वमा वैध वदलाव नआएमा सरकारीकरणको चरणमा प्रवेश गर्ने निश्वित छ ।

उसोतः एनसेल प्रकरणमा नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआइबी)ले ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात जस्ता विषयमा अनुसन्धान भने गरिरहेको छ। सर्वोच्चले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व सरकारको नाममा आउने बाटो खुला गरिदिएपनि कानूनी बाटाहरु कसरी अघि बढ्छन्? सरकारी नीति कस्ता बन्छन भन्ने विषयले समेत यो विषयमा थप निर्धारण गर्नेछ ।

अमरेशको सक्रियता

तत्कालीन समयमा स्वतन्त्र रुपमा प्रतिनिधिसभामा निर्वाचित भएका अमरेशकुमार सिंहले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई चुनौती दिदै सर्वोच्चमा रिट दर्ता गराए। अमरेश अहिले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीबाट कांग्रेस सभापति गगन थापालाई पराजित गर्दै फेरि सर्लाही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र नम्बर ४ बाट प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्यमा निर्वाचित भइसकेका छन्।

उनै सिंहले सर्वोच्चमा एनसेल आजियाटा, दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय, ठूला करदाता कार्यालय, कम्पनी रजिष्ट्रार जस्ता धेरै निकायलाई विपक्षी बनाएर रिट दर्ता गराएका थिए। यहि प्रकरणमा सर्वोच्चको फैसलाले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अवैध ठहर गरेको हो।

निर्णय अब सरकारको हातमा

नेपालमा विदेशी लगानीका सम्बन्धमा अनेक अफवाहहरु फैलिने गर्छन्। कतिपयले एनसेल प्रकरणले नेपालमा ठूला लगानी नआउने भन्दै यसलाई मोड्ने प्रयास समेत गरेको देखिन्छ। सरकारले पनि मध्यम वर्गलाई ठूलो प्रभाव पर्ने गरि काम गरिरहेको बेला विदेशी लगानीलाई नेपालको कानूनको पालना गर्ने र विवादको समाधानका निम्ति सहजीकरणको बाटो खोज्दै काम गर्ने वातावरण सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।

एनसेल कब्जा गर्ने सतिसलालसहितको टोलीले नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा लिलाम सकारेको घटनाबाटै सरकारले कानूनको पालना गराउने र आवश्यक सहजीकरणसहित दण्ड र पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्न आवश्यक देखिन्छ। तर, सरकारले यस्ता विषयलाई कसरी अघि लैजान्छ भन्ने चासो र केहि शंकाहरु भने देखिन्छन। यद्यपी अब कानूनविपरितका विषयलाई दण्ड र विदेशी लगानीलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने गरि काम गर्नुको विकल्प भने देखिन्न ।

articles.title: कोलकाताबाट २४ घण्टामै नेपालमा ढुवानी, व्यवसायी उत्साहित
articles.summary:
मोरङ । उद्घाटन भएको करिब ३ वर्षपछि विराटनगरस्थित एकीकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधन पछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपालको कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो ।

विराटनगर स्थित एकिकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । तत्कालिन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले २०८० साल जेठ १८ गते उद्घाटन गरेयता कार्गो रेल आउन सकेको थिएन ।

मोरङको नेमुवास्थित स्वस्तिक आयल इण्डष्ट्रिजले मगाएको तोरी बोकेका ४० वटा कन्टेनरसहितको कार्गो रेल नेपाल भंसार यार्डसम्म आएको हो । रेल आएपछि सुनसरी मोरङ औद्योगिक करिडोरका उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरु उत्साहित भएका छन् ।

कार्गो रेलबाट ढुवानी गर्दा ढुवानी लागत २५ देखि ३० प्रतिशत घट्ने, कोलकाता बन्दरगाहबाट विराटनगरसम्म २४ घण्टामा सामान आईपुग्ने र बाटोमा सामान चोरी हुने समस्या निराकरण हुने भएकाले अन्य क्षेत्रका उद्योगहरुसँग प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सहज हुने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

भारत सरकार अन्र्तर्गतको कन्कोर अर्थात कन्टेनर कर्पोरेशन अफ इण्डिया लिमिटेडको कार्गाे रेलबाट सोमवार एनसिवाई अर्थात नेपाल कस्टम यार्ड सम्म मालवाहक रेल आएको हो ।

कन्कोरका प्रतिनिधि संजिव साहले हप्तामा दुई दिन कोलकाताबाट विराटनगरसम्म कार्गो रेल संचालन गर्ने र यसलाई आवश्यकता अनुसार बढाउदै लैजाने जानकारी दिए ।

पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधनपछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपाल कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो । कार्गो रेल संचालन पछि विराटनगर आएको कन्टेनर खाली फर्कने भएकाले यहाँबाट वस्तु निर्यातमा पनि सहजता आउने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

articles.title: प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालद्वारा ‘Soirée Francaise’ आयोजना: फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति र जीवनशैलीको अनुभव
articles.summary:
अग्नि ग्रुप अन्तर्गतको प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालले ‘Soirée Française – A Night of French Elegance’ शीर्षकमा एक विशेष 'फ्रेन्च फाइन डाइनिङ' कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न गरेको छ। काठमाडौँस्थित ला टेरास (La Terrasse) मा आयोजना गरिएको उक्त कार्यक्रममा प्युजोका विशिष्ट ग्राहक, व्यावसायिक साझेदार तथा फ्रान्सेली संस्कृतिप्रति आत्मियता राख्ने अतिथिहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रमले फ्रान्सको समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत र त्यसको प्रेरणादायी भावनालाई सम्मान गर्दै आपसी सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने उद्देश्य राखेको थियो।

विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीको भावनाबाट प्रेरित

सन् २०२६ को फिफा विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीले प्रदर्शन गरेको समर्पण, दृढता, उत्कृष्टता र एकताको भावनाबाट प्रेरित भई यो कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको हो। खेलको नतिजाभन्दा माथि उठेर फ्रान्सेली खेल संस्कृतिको अदम्य भावना र त्यसको विरासतलाई सम्मान गर्नु कार्यक्रमको मुख्य पक्ष थियो। यी मूल्यहरू प्युजो ब्रान्डको दीर्घकालीन पहिचानसँग समेत मेल खाने भएकाले सोही भावनालाई कार्यक्रममा प्रतिबिम्बित गरिएको थियो।

नेटवर्किङ र प्रिमियम जीवनशैलीको अनुभव

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी अतिथिहरूले पेरिस-प्रेरित आकर्षक सजावट तथा आत्मीय वातावरणमा विविध परम्परागत फ्रेन्च परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै नेटवर्किङको अनुभव सँगालेका थिए। प्युजोको फ्रान्सेली सम्पदालाई झल्काउँदै आफ्ना ग्राहकहरूप्रति कृतज्ञता व्यक्त गर्न र नेपालमा प्युजो समुदायसँगको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउन यस अवसरले सहयोग पुर्‍याएको कम्पनीले जनाएको छ।

ग्राहक केन्द्रित प्रतिबद्धता

यस अवसरमा प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूले गुणस्तरीय गतिशीलता (मोबिलिटी) समाधानका साथै ग्राहकलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको जीवनशैली अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने र विश्वव्यापी रूपमा प्युजोले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूल्य एवम् परम्परालाई निरन्तर अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता पुनः व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रमको समापन फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति, मित्रता र उत्कृष्टताको साझा भावनाप्रति सम्मान व्यक्त गर्दै ‘टोस्ट’ (Toast) का साथ गरिएको थियो। सहभागीहरूले यस अविस्मरणीय अनुभवले प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपाल र ग्राहकहरूबीचको प्रिमियम सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाएको विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन्

articles.title: राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस घोषणा गर्न इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनको माग
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलन प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । गत वर्षको भदौ २३ र २४ गते देशमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोह र त्यसक्रममा भएका गम्भीर मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटनासम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघ पुगेको छ ।

नेपालभित्र प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न चौतर्फी माग भइरहेका बेला आयोगले करिब १० हजार पृष्ठ लामो उक्त प्रतिवेदन जेनेभास्थित मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा पेश गरेको छ।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली र गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखकसहित उच्च अधिकारीहरूमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धानको सिफारिस गरिएको यो प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पुगेसँगै अब सरकारमाथि कूटनीतिक र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढ्ने देखिएको छ ।

गएको भदौ २३–२४ गतेको जेनजी विद्रोहसम्बन्धी राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघीय मानव अधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय ओएचसीएचआर जेनेभामा पेश भएको छ ।

यो प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अब सरकारलाई थप दबाब पर्नेछ । जुन १५ देखि जुलाइ ७ सम्म जेनेभामा चलेको ह्युमन राइट काउन्सिलको २४औँ बैठक र ६२ औँ सत्रमा राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगका सदस्य मिहिर ठाकुरले नेपालमा भएको जेनजी विद्रोहको मानवअधिकार अवस्थाका विस्तृत विवरणसहितको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि सरकारलाई बुझाएको जानकारी दिँदै सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वय गर्नैपर्ने जानकारी गराएका थिए ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार आयोगले पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनलाई नोटमा राखेको छ । सरकारलाई मानवअधिकार आयोगको प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनका लागि अरु दबाब पर्नेछ । जेनेभा बैठकमा भाग लिन आयोगका सदस्य ठाकुरसँगै आयोगकी उपसचिव माया शर्मा पनि पुगेकी थिइन ।

सरकारमाथि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दबाब बढाउने रणनीति

आयोगभित्रैका केही अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगर्ने आशंका बढेपछि आयोगले प्रतिवेदन अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मञ्चमा पठाएको हो ।

नेपालमै प्रतिवेदन पूर्णरूपमा सार्वजनिक गर्न आग्रह मानव अधिकार आयोगले आग्रह गरे पनि त्यो सम्भव नभएको बताउने गरेकाले पनि अब जेनेभाबाटै थप प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढ्न सक्ने अवस्था बनेको छ ।

प्रतिवेदनमा को–कोमाथि अनुसन्धान सिफारिस ?

जेनजी आन्दोलनमा भएको दमन, गोली प्रहार, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी तथा विध्वंसका घटनाबारे आयेगको प्रतिवेदन करिब १० हजार पृष्ठको छ । तर आयोगले प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश मात्रै सार्वजनिक गरेको थियो ।

उक्त प्रतिवेदनमा तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री केपी शर्मा ओली, तत्कालीन गृहमन्त्री रमेश लेखक, तत्कालीन सञ्चारमन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङ, तत्कालीन प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक चन्द्रकुवेर खापुङ लगायतमाथि फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएको छ ।

यसैगरी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएको विध्वंसमा कलाकार, पत्रकार, इन्फ्लुएन्सर तथा हाल संसद् र सरकारमा रहेका केही व्यक्तिहरूमाथि पनि थप अनुसन्धान गर्न आयोगले सिफारिस गरेको छ ।

आन्दोलनका घटनाबारे आयोगको निष्कर्ष

पूर्ण प्रतिवेदनमा भदौ २३ देखि २६ सम्मका घटना समेटिएका छन् । कसले कोसँग संवाद ग¥यो ?के–के कुरा भयो ? सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगो लगाउनेसम्ममा कसको योजना थियो भन्ने समेटिएका छन् ।

भीड कसरी उग्र बन्यो, सार्वजनिक सम्पत्तिमा आगजनी गर्ने योजना कसरी बनेको थियो भन्ने विवरण पनि प्रतिवेदनमा समावेश छ । आयोगले अनुसन्धानका लागि आवश्यक केही प्रमाण, विशेषगरी गोलीका अवशेष बुलेट संकलन गर्न नसकिएको स्वीकार गरेको छ ।

ओली–लेखकले नै मागेका छन्, प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि

आयोगको पूर्ण प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक गर्न माग भइरहँदा फौजदारी अनुसन्धान अघि बढाउन सिफारिस गरिएका पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री एवम् एमाले अध्यक्ष ओली, पूर्व गृहमन्त्री एवम् कांग्रेस नेता रमेश लेखक, पूर्व सञ्चार मन्त्री पृथ्वी सुब्बा गुरुङले प्रतिवेदनमाथि प्रश्न उठाउँदै आयोगसमक्ष निवेदन दर्ता गराएका छन् ।

प्रतिवेदनको केही अंश झिकिएको र केही अंश थपिएको आशंकापछि उनीहरुले प्रतिवेदन माग गरेका हुन् । ओलीको तर्फबाट छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिवेदन माग गर्दै एमाले नेता महेश बर्तौलाले असार १२ गते आयोगमा निवेदन दर्ता गराएका थिए ।

ओलीले आयोगको बैठकको निर्णय नम्बर १७७ को प्रमाणित प्रतिलिपि, लिली थापा नेतृत्वको समितिले आयोगमा पेश गरेको प्रतिवेदनको प्रतिलिपि, प्रतिवेदनमा थपघट गरिएको अंश र थपघट गर्नुको कारणसमेत माग गरेका छन् ।

यस्तै, रास्वपा सभापति रवि लामिछानेलाई कारागारबाट बाहिर निकाल्न गएको आरोप लागेका सांसद दीपक बोहोराले पनि आयोगमा निवेदन दिएका थिए । आयोगले भनेको समयमा आफू अस्पतालमा रहेको उनको दलिल छ ।

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयमा प्रतिवेदन पेश भएपछि के हुन्छ ?

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको मानवअधिकार उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालयले अब चार चरणमा प्रक्रिया अघि बढाउँछ ।

पहिलो चरण : अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखः–

प्रतिवेदन संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघको आधिकारिक अभिलेखमा दर्ता हुन्छ । यसले नेपालमा मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन भएको दाबी अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय निगरानीमा प्रवेश गर्छ ।

दोस्रो चरण : प्रश्न र स्पष्टीकरणः–

मानव अधिकार परिषद्का सदस्य राष्ट्रहरूले नेपाल सरकारसँग स्पष्टीकरण माग्न सक्छन् ।

तेस्रो चरण : सिफारिसः–

उच्चायुक्तको कार्यालय वा विशेष प्रतिवेदकहरूले नेपाललाई अनुसन्धान, पीडितलाई क्षतिपूर्ति वा जिम्मेवार व्यक्तिमाथि कारबाही गर्न सिफारिस गर्न सक्छन् ।

चौथो चरण : निगरानीः–

नेपालले ती सिफारिस कार्यान्वयन ग¥यो कि गरेन भनेर आगामी सत्रहरूमा पुनःसमीक्षा हुन्छ ।

जेनजी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयनमा दबाब

जेनजी आन्दोलनको प्रतिवेदन अब नेपालको आन्तरिक राजनीतिक विवाद मात्र रहेन, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानव अधिकार बहसको विषय बनेको छ । मानव अधिकार परिषद्को ६२औँ सत्रमा यसबारे औपचारिक जानकारी प्रस्तुत भइसकेकाले नेपाल सरकारले प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेमा आगामी सत्रहरूमा थप प्रश्न उठ्न सक्छन् ।

यद्यपी प्रतिवेदन कार्यान्वयन नगरेकै कारण कुनै देशलाई तुरुन्त प्रतिबन्ध भने लाग्दैन ।तर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय आलोचना बढ्छ । मानव अधिकार सम्बन्धी वार्षिक प्रतिवेदनमा नकारात्मक उल्लेख हुन्छ । यसको असरले वैदेशिक सहायता र विकास साझेदारहरूको दबाब बढ्न सक्छ ।

त्यस्तै, विशेष प्रतिवेदक वा अनुसन्धान टोली पठाउने सम्भावना पनि रहन्छ। नेपालमा विगतमा द्वन्द्वकालीन मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका विषयमा संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघले पटक–पटक चासो व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

यस्ता घटनामा कुन कुन देशलाई प्रतिबन्ध लागेको छ ?

मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनका आधारमा विभिन्न देशहरूमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको उदाहरणहरु छन् । म्यानमारमा सैन्य दमन र मानव अधिकार उल्लंघनको घटनामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ भने इरानमा प्रदर्शनकारीमाथि दमन गरेको भन्दै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघन भएको निश्कर्षमा प्रतिबन्ध लगाइएको छ।

त्यस्तै मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका घटना छानबिन गरेर कारवाही नगरेका कारण बेलारुस, गृहयुद्ध र मानवअधिकार उल्लंघनका कारण सिरिया लगायतका देश प्रतिबन्धमा परेका छन् ।

articles.title: झापाका ४२ परिवार तनावमा, अन्तिम किस्ता रोकिएपछि छटपटि
articles.summary:
झापा । झापाको मेचीनगरस्थित दिपज्योती टोलका ४२ परिवार दुई दशकअघि किस्ताबन्दीमा खरिद गरेको जग्गाको लालपूर्जा नपाउँदा समस्यामा परेका छन् । मेचीनगर २ र ३ को सिमानास्थित जग्गा हालसम्म नामसारी हुन नसक्दा पीडित परिवारको समस्या झन् जटिल बन्दै गएको छ ।

झापाको मेचीनगर ३ स्थित बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहेको चिया बगान नभएको खाली जग्गा वि.स २०६३÷०६४ सालमा शुभ चिया प्रालिले बैना गरि घरघडेरीका लागि स्थानीयलाई किस्ताबन्दी एकदेखि पाँच कठ्ठासम्म बिक्री प्रक्रिया अगाडी बढायो ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारलाई लक्षित गरी बिक्री गरिएको उक्त जग्गाको अधिकांश किस्ता तिरे पनि अन्तिम किस्ता लिएपछि लालपूर्जा उपलब्ध गराउने सहमति कार्यान्वयन नभएको पीडितहरूको भनाइ छ ।

अन्तिम किस्ता पनि तिर्न तयार भएका उनीहरुको संस्थाले रकम नै लिएन । अहिले उनीहरुको न पैसा फिर्ता भएको छ, न लालपूर्जा नै पाएका छन् ।

त्यस्तै पीडित स्थानीयका अनुसार जग्गा बजगाई टि–स्टेट प्रालिको नाममा रहे पनि तत्कालीन शुभ चिया प्रालिका अध्यक्ष हेमराज भारतीले कारोबार अगाडी बढाएका थिए । तर उनले पैसा लिएपछि त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न आलटाल गरेको दुखेसो पीडित पोख्छन् । उनीहरुले जग्गा समस्या तत्काल समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग माग गरेका छन्।

यता शुभ चिया प्रालिका वर्तमान अध्यक्ष रमेश दाहालले विगतमा कारोबार संस्थागत प्रक्रियाअनुसार नभएकाले समस्या उत्पन्न भएको बताउँछन् । समस्या समाधानका लागि सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायसँग आवश्यक गृहकार्य भइरहेको र पीडितलाई न्याय दिलाउने प्रयास जारी रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

सुकुम्बासी तथा न्यून आय भएका परिवारले साहुसंग ऋण गरेर किस्ता वापतको रकम समेत दिइ सकेको अवस्थामा अन्तिम किस्ता नलिई जग्गाको स्वामित्व समेत प्रदान नगर्दा ४२ परिवार समस्यामा परेका छन् । तसर्थ उनीहरुलाई सम्बन्धित सरोकारवाला निकायले यथाशिघ्र समस्या समाधान गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यक देखिन्छ ।

articles.title: नेपाल लाइफको ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान, १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा आर्जन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालको सर्वाधिक विश्वासिलो जीवन बीमा कम्पनीका रूपमा स्थापित नेपाल लाइफ इन्स्योरेन्सले आफ्नो २५ वर्षको गौरवमय यात्रा (सिल्भर जुबिली) का अवसरमा रु. १३ अर्बभन्दा बढी प्रथम बीमा शुल्क (FPI) आर्जन गर्दै जीवन बीमा इतिहासमा नयाँ ऐतिहासिक कीर्तिमान कायम गरेको छ।

गत आर्थिक वर्षमा रु. १० अर्ब प्रथम बीमा शुल्क आर्जन गरेको कम्पनीले यस वर्ष उक्त उपलब्धिलाई अझ उचाइमा पुर्‍याउँदै बीमा उद्योगमा नयाँ मानक स्थापित गरेको हो।

यस ऐतिहासिक सफलताका अवसरमा कम्पनीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रमण पराजुलीले सम्पूर्ण बीमित, अभिकर्ता, कर्मचारी, शेयरधनी तथा सरोकारवालाहरू प्रति आभार व्यक्त गर्दै आगामी दिनमा अझ थप प्रविधिमैत्री सेवा, नवीन बीमा योजना र उत्कृष्ट सेवा प्रदान गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे ।

articles.title: सिद्धार्थ बैंकद्वारा ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सुविधा सञ्चालनमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सिद्धार्थ बैंक लिमिटेडले ग्राहकहरुको तत्कालको वित्तीय आवश्यकतालाई सहज र सर्वसुलभ बनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ नयाँ कर्जा योजना ‘सिद्धार्थ गोल्ड लोन’ सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

यस योजना अन्तर्गत ग्राहकहरुले आफ्नो सुन तथा सुनका गरगहनाहरु धितो राखी बैंकबाट अधिकतम रु. ५० लाखसम्मको कर्जा रकम प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्, जसमा धितो सुनको मूल्यांकनका आधारमा बढीमा ७५ प्रतिशतसम्म कर्जा प्रवाह गरिनेछ।

ग्राहकहरूले आफ्नो व्यक्तिगत तथा व्यावसायिक आवश्यकता सहज रूपमा पूरा गर्न सकुन् भन्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको यो सुरक्षित र भरपर्दो सुविधा हालका लागि बैंकको काठमाडौंस्थित न्यूरोड गेट शाखाबाट उपलब्ध छ, र यस सम्बन्धी थप जानकारीका लागि बैंकको २४ सै घण्टा सञ्चालनमा रहने ग्राहक सेवा केन्द्र ‘सिद्धार्थ केयर’ मा सम्पर्क गर्न सकिनेछ।

articles.title: कतारमा नेपाली समुदायद्वारा स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली
articles.summary:
कतार । गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) राष्ट्रिय समन्वय परिषद् (एनसीसी) कतारले स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस फादर अमिर शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्न शोकसभा आयोजना गरेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व तथा कतारको समृद्धि, विकास र विश्वमञ्चमा स्थापित गराउन पुर्‍याएको अतुलनीय योगदानको उच्च सम्मान गरिएको थियो।

कार्यक्रममा कतारस्थित नेपाली राजदूतावासका कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेल प्रमुख अतिथिका रूपमा सहभागी भएका थिए। साथै कतारमा क्रियाशील विभिन्न नेपाली सामाजिक तथा कल्याणकारी संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेखनीय उपस्थिति रहेको थियो। शोकको यस घडीमा नेपाली समुदायले एकता र ऐक्यबद्धता प्रदर्शन गरेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रमको सुरुआत पवित्र कुरआनको तिलावतबाट भएको थियो भने मौलाना गुलाम नबी रजबीले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको आत्माको चिरशान्तिको कामना गर्दै कतार राज्यको शान्ति, स्थायित्व र समृद्धिका लागि विशेष दुआ गरेका थिए।

एनआरएनए एनसीसी कतारका अध्यक्ष कृष्ण पन्थीले स्वागत मन्तव्य दिँदै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको निधनप्रति गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गरे।

उनले कतारका अमिर, राजपरिवार, सरकार तथा सम्पूर्ण कतारी जनताप्रति समवेदना व्यक्त गर्दै स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व, राष्ट्र निर्माणमा खेलेको ऐतिहासिक भूमिका र उनले छोडेको प्रेरणादायी विरासतको प्रशंसा गरे। पन्थीले कतारलाई विश्वकै सम्मानित र समृद्ध राष्ट्रका रूपमा स्थापित गर्न फादर अमिरको योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहेको बताए।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख वक्ता प्राध्यापक मोहम्मद रमजान अली मियाँले नेपाल–कतारबीचको लामो समयदेखिको मित्रवत सम्बन्ध र बढ्दो सहकार्यबारे चर्चा गरे। उनले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरको नेतृत्वमा कतारले आर्थिक विविधीकरण, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य, पूर्वाधार विकास तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कूटनीतिमा उल्लेखनीय प्रगति हासिल गरेको बताए। साथै कतारले हजारौँ नेपालीलाई रोजगारी तथा अवसर उपलब्ध गराउँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे।

कतारस्थित नेपाली दूतावासका तर्फबाट बोल्दै कूटनीतिज्ञ प्रेमप्रसाद पोखरेलले स्वर्गीय फादर अमिरप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै उनको योगदानको उच्च प्रशंसा गरे।

उनले नेपाल–कतारबीचको मैत्रीपूर्ण सम्बन्ध निरन्तर सुदृढ हुँदै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै आगामी दिनमा दुई देशबीचको सहयोग र मित्रतालाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी विभिन्न नेपाली संघ–संस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले पनि शोक मन्तव्य व्यक्त गर्दै कतारले नेपाली समुदायलाई प्रदान गरेको अवसरप्रति आभार प्रकट गरे। साथै कठिन घडीमा कतारका नेतृत्व र जनताप्रति ऐक्यबद्धता तथा सम्मान व्यक्त गरे।

श्रद्धाञ्जली सभा अन्त्यमा स्वर्गीय हिज हाइनेस शेख हमद बिन खलिफा अल थानीको सम्मानमा सामूहिक प्रार्थना तथा एक मिनेट मौनधारण गरिएको थियो। कार्यक्रममा वक्ताहरूले उनको दूरदर्शी नेतृत्व र योगदानले आगामी पुस्तालाई पनि प्रेरणा दिइरहने विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका थिए।

articles.title: Nepal’s Rs146 billion edible oil exports to India under scrutiny over tariff advantage
articles.summary:
Nepal exported 704,844 tonnes of refined soyabean, palm and sunflower oil worth Rs146 billion to India in the last fiscal year, even though it produces only a negligible amount of the raw materials. Experts say the trade is a classic example of a rent-seeking business that exploits tariff differentials rather than generating genuine domestic value.

The rapid growth of edible oil exports has raised concerns in both Nepal and India. Nepal spends dollars importing crude edible oils from third countries but earns Indian rupees by exporting refined products to India. Indian vegetable oil producers, meanwhile, argue that duty-free imports from Nepal are undercutting their domestic processing industry.

According to a report published in the Financial Express newspaper, the Indian Vegetable Oil Producers' Association (IVPA) wrote to Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday, saying the recent surge in duty-free refined edible oil imports, particularly from Nepal, exposed a failure of India's preferential trade arrangements.

Nepal's overall exports increased by 13.81 percent to Rs315.29 billion in the last fiscal year, which ended in mid-July. Refined edible oils alone accounted for nearly half of the country's total exports.

The trade is largely driven by tariff arbitrage.

Nepal imports crude soyabean, sunflower and palm oil from countries such as Argentina, Indonesia, Brazil, Malaysia and Ukraine, refines the oils domestically, and re-exports them duty-free to India under the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) and the Nepal-India Trade Treaty.

India imposes a 35.75 percent import duty on refined edible oils from non-SAFTA countries.

However, Nepal, as a least developed country, enjoys zero or highly preferential duty rates on its refined oil exports.

Indian industry bodies, including the IVPA and the Solvent Extractors' Association (SEA), have argued that actual local value addition in Nepal is only around 5 to 7 percent, well short of SAFTA's 30 percent domestic value-addition requirement.

Sudhakar Desai, president of the IVPA, told the Financial Express that the preferential treatment had driven a sharp increase in imports of refined soyabean and palm oil from Nepal, making Indian refiners more vulnerable.

Several reports have questioned whether Nepal's edible oil exports generate meaningful economic benefits, noting that value addition remains limited while employment generation is relatively low.

The IVPA says the value added in converting crude oil into refined oil is only 5 to 7 percent.

Combined with Nepal's duty concessions on imported crude oil and India's zero-duty access for Nepali refined products, this creates a significant cost advantage over Indian processors.

Diwakar Raj Pandey, secretariat chief of the Nepal Vegetable Ghee and Oil Manufacturers Association, defended the industry, saying most edible oil factories in Nepal are export-oriented because domestic consumption is too small to absorb their production.

"If exports are halted, many factories will have no choice but to shut down," Pandey said. "The industry complies with the value-addition provision."

According to the association, Nepal has 27 edible oil manufacturing plants employing around 15,000 people directly and indirectly.

Indian media reports say the country imports about 57 percent of its annual edible oil requirement of 24-25 million tonnes. India imports crude palm oil mainly from Malaysia and Indonesia, while crude soyabean and sunflower oils come from Argentina, Brazil, Russia and Ukraine.

Indian edible oil producers have repeatedly urged their government to regulate imports from Nepal.

In February 2025, the SEA asked the Indian government to regulate edible oil imports from Nepal and other SAARC countries, claiming that the imports violated rules of origin, bypassed trade regulations, and hurt India's refiners, farmers and government revenue.

Nepal's edible oil exports accelerated after India raised the import duty on refined edible oils to 35.75 percent in September 2024 and increased the duty on crude edible oils to 16.5 percent in May 2025.

Since then, Nepal's edible oil exports to India have grown by more than 15 percent annually.

Nepal exported 704,844 tonnes of refined soyabean, palm and sunflower oil worth Rs146.05 billion to India in the last fiscal year. During the same period, it imported 1.01 million tonnes of crude soyabean, palm and sunflower oil worth Rs168.27 billion.

Exports of refined soyabean oil, Nepal's largest export item, increased by 20 percent to Rs128.74 billion.

The country imported 801,296 tonnes of crude soyabean oil worth Rs132.76 billion during the review period, generating Rs5.63 billion in customs revenue. Nepal imposes a 5 percent Agriculture Service Reform Fee on specified imported agricultural products. Most crude soyabean oil came from Argentina and Brazil, followed by China and Paraguay.

Exports of refined palm oil surged by 253.16 percent to Rs8.37 billion. Nepal exported 41,676 tonnes of refined palm oil during the fiscal year.

The country imported 85,986 tonnes of crude palm oil worth Rs13.73 billion, generating Rs1.22 billion in customs revenue. Most imports came from Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.

Nepal also imports refined edible oil for domestic consumption. During the review period, it imported 34,303 tonnes of refined palm oil worth Rs5.88 billion, mainly from Malaysia and Indonesia.

Exports of refined sunflower oil, however, fell by 27.43 percent to Rs8.94 billion.

Nepal imported 127,487 tonnes of crude sunflower oil worth Rs21.77 billion during the fiscal year, generating Rs3.56 billion in revenue. Most crude sunflower oil came from Argentina and Ukraine.

Economist Chandra Mani Adhikari said Nepal has derived limited economic benefit from the edible oil trade because the country does not produce the underlying raw materials.

"Even if India restricts edible oil imports from Nepal, it will mainly reduce Nepal's export figures, which have surged in recent years," Adhikari said. "The government will also lose some customs revenue."

He warned that India could impose duties or quantitative restrictions on imports from Nepal at any time.

"If this trade is eventually curtailed, Nepal should focus on promoting exports of products it genuinely produces, such as tea, ginger and large cardamom," Adhikari said. "That would create more sustainable trade and deliver greater long-term benefits to the economy."

articles.title: How Nepali para-swimmers are turning tragic negligence into a shot at Asian Para Games glory
articles.summary:
What are the basics of swimming? Hands and legs maybe.

But when Jenisha Kadayat, Harka Man Gharti and Member Singi Syangba stood at the edge of the pool at the Refresh Recreation Centre in Bauddha on Friday morning, they lacked what most would consider the bare basics.

Kadayat warmed up from her wheelchair, her body immobile below the waist due to a spinal cord injury. Gharti, who has no arms, stretched his legs and torso, while Syangba—his left leg amputated below the knee—hopped on one foot to maintain his balance as he went through his warm-up routine.

As the trio waited for coach Subha Shrestha’s whistle, Kadayat was already afloat in the lane since she could not stand, while able-bodied swimmers nearby and gym-goers on the floor above, who saw the trio for the first time, watched in amazement: How can they swim?

But the moment the whistle blew for a 100-metre swim, their doubts evaporated. Gharti and Syangba sliced into the water with sharp dives, while Kadayat propelled herself forward, her stroke clean and powerful. They weren’t just swimming; they were executing laps like professionals along the 25-metre-long pool.

The trio was training for the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games, scheduled for October in Japan.

“We have four swimmers preparing to represent the country,” said Saroj Shrestha, president of the Nepal Para Swimming Association. “Srijana Sarki is our fourth, though she missed today’s session.”

The squad has been training at the Boudha facility for about five months—a location chosen largely out of necessity.

“Finding an accessible pool for para-athletes is exceptionally hard,” Shrestha explained. “The swimming complex in Satdobato is simply too far for them to commute regularly. We are deeply grateful to this centre for giving us pool access at a heavy discount.”

Except on weekends, their one-hour training session kicks off precisely at 7:30am.

Getting there is quite a for these swimmers. Kadayat, who lives in a hostel in Jorpati, arrives on a scooter retrofitted with auxiliary support wheels to navigate the Kathmandu traffic. Gharti and Syangba, who walks with a prosthetic leg, arrive on foot, as they live within a ten-minute walk from the venue.

But their journey to this pool started much further away—and in ways none could have anticipated.

Injured by someone else’s negligence

Kadayat was riding her bicycle home in Kailali’s Gauriganga Municipality, her mind drifting through ordinary thoughts. Then, in a split second, a tree crashed down on her, altering her life forever.

“It was on November 2, 2013,” recalls Kadayat, now 26. The date is etched in her memory. “Some people were chopping down a tree. There were no warning signs to alert passersby, and no one standing by to tell people to stop. The tree fell on top of me. The next thing I knew was that I had lost all movement in the lower half of my body from a spinal cord injury.”

A couple of years later, around the time of the devastating April 2015 earthquake, Gharti’s life took another tragic turn.

“I was just a kid back then,” recalls the 21-year-old native of Baglung. “We used to play and herd cattle near an under-construction hydropower site. One day I grabbed an insulator—something I had touched many times before—without knowing the power had been switched on. I was severely electrocuted. There was no fencing, no warning signs, nothing to keep us away.”

Syangba, on the other hand, was working in the transport sector at the Kerung border crossing between Nepal and China in Rasuwa district. The year was 2017.

“I was standing beside our truck on the side of the road when another truck hit me,” Syangba shared. “My left leg was crushed so badly that it had to be amputated below the knee. Because the accident happened right in the border zone, no authorities on either side ever filed a case or initiated legal proceedings.”

Without any legal accountability, none of the three received compensation from those responsible for their accidents. Saroj Shrestha, president of the Nepal Para Swimming Association, noted that their journey from injury to elite training was borne entirely out of personal endurance.

“None of the trio received any financial support from the authorities and covered their treatment on their own,” Saroj said. “They lost their abilities, but have dedicated themselves to a bigger goal. We are glad they took up a sport and decided to make their name as they still have a lot of fire in them.”

Swimming changed their lives

“When I first lost mobility, people around me said I would have been better off dead. At my lowest, I even tried to take my life a couple of times,” Kadayat said, with a subtle grin as she recounted a struggle she had overcome. “When I told my family and neighbours that I wanted to become a swimmer, they were simply shocked.”

Their concern wasn’t entirely misplaced. Even before her accident, Kadayat had nearly drowned a few times as a child and never knew how to swim.

“I finally took the plunge about nine years ago,” she recalled. “And ever since, the pool has been my solace. I feel completely normal the moment I enter one.”

Kadayat also argued that swimming has improved her physical and mental health. “I feel strong mentally. While swimming, my legs mobilise in the water; it improves blood circulation,” she adds.

Syangba had travelled to Kathmandu for a prosthetic leg when a doctor suggested he try swimming.

“In water, I found a renewed purpose,” he said. “It gave me a reason to push for more in life.”

Gharti, meanwhile, has lived in Kathmandu ever since losing his arms—moving to the Capital to access both specialised medical care and accessible education.

“I went to a pool with a group of friends from my hostel, and they urged me to give it a shot,” Gharti recalled. “That was about seven years ago. Today, swimming is an integral part of my life.”

Beyond athletic performance, all three emphasise that swimming restored their self-respect and mental drive. That confidence extends past the pool deck: all three are actively pursuing higher education.

Kadayat is currently in the third semester of the Master in Public Administration at Jana Prasashan Campus in Balkhu. Syangba recently earned his Bachelor’s in Education from Kalika Himalaya Campus in Rasuwa. Gharti, having just completed high school, plans to study computer science.

“I can operate a computer or laptop using my toes,” Gharti said, effortlessly lifting his foot to demonstrate how his toes manoeuvre across a keyboard.

No state support for para swimmers

Syangba moved to Kathmandu five months ago specifically to prepare for the Asian Para Games. Back home in Rasuwa, consistent training is impossible.

“There is an outdoor pool near my home, but without heating, I can’t use it,” Syangba explained. “Because of my amputation, my body doesn’t tolerate cold water.”

Even the Capital has a dearth of temperature-controlled facilities.

“Not every swimming facility is welcoming or accessible for athletes with disabilities,” said coach Subha. “Cold water is a major health issue for them. Here in Boudha, the indoor pool stays around 26-27 degrees Celcius. Even so, they cannot manage to train throughout the week.”

Despite these persistent obstacles, the trio has consistently found ways to adapt and excel.

They are also no strangers to the international stage. It was their standout performance at the Para Swimming World Series in Japan last year that punched their tickets to the Asian Para Games.

“All three completed their races under the required minimum qualifying times,” said Saroj, who rarely misses a morning training session. “They are aiming for major results on the continent’s biggest stage, all while operating with no state resources.”

Even now, the Para Swimming Association relies almost entirely on private goodwill to keep the lights on and the pool access paid for.

“There is zero support from the government. We survive on contributions from well-wishers,” Shrestha added. “If we could secure stable financial backing to properly resource their training, I firmly believe our swimmers could compete with the very best in the world.”

But the swimmers insist that state neglect will not hold them back when they step onto the block in Japan.

“It isn’t just para-athletes who are neglected in Nepali sports. Almost every athlete faces this,” the trio conferred. “In a situation like this, proving what we can do with actual results on the international stage will make our success feel sweeter.”

Gharti stressed that he was not going to Japan merely to attend the Asian event. “I told our association officials … ‘If I am going, that’s for bringing the medal’,” Gharti told the Post with a wink of determination.

At the Asian Para Games, Kadayat, Gharti, Syangba and Sarki will be competing in the 50-metre and 100-metre freestyle categories. Besides, Gharti is competing in the 50-metre butterfly event as well.

Kadayat falls in the S6 category while Gharti is in S5 and Syangba in S10. “Srijana’s classification is yet to arrive. But she is also suffering from spinal cord injury and is most likely to compete in the S6 category,” said Saroj Shrestha.

And with determination to do better the next day, the trio left the pool for home. Syangba and Gharti said they would have rest for a while, while Kadayat rushed to the hostel, where she’d have her lunch and then ride to Banasthali—to the Rastriya Swatantra Party office. She has been working as a receptionist for around three years.

articles.title: Nepal returns to French firm to procure automated biometric system licences
articles.summary:
The government has decided to procure 10 million Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) units from the French firm IN Groupe, the parent company of IDEMIA, for the Department of National Identity and Civil Registration without competitive bidding.

The Balendra Shah-led Cabinet, in its June 12 meeting, decided to procure the Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) through a government-to-government agreement and direct purchase from the French company, based on a proposal submitted by the Department of National ID and Civil Registration under the Ministry of Home Affairs. As per the Cabinet decision, out of the 10 million units, 1.5 million will be procured directly from the company and the rest of the ABIS units will come under a government-to-government deal.

The licence for the ABIS system is about to expire, with the NID having a stock of over some thousands of biometric identification systems in its vault.

Previously, the department purchased ABIS licences from Safran, a private French company. With the licences sold by IDEMIA close to expiry, the department is preparing to procure them from IN Groupe, the parent company of Safran and IDEMIA.

IDEMIA has been providing passports to Nepal since 2010. Safran Identity, which earlier supplied the ABIS system to the department, has been taken over by the IN Groupe.

“After the Cabinet decision, the home ministry has formed a negotiation team to deal with the IN Groupe,” Krishna Poudel, director general at the department, told the Post. The cost of each ABIS would be equal to what the department had proposed, he said.

An ABIS licence is a software authorisation contract that allows governments or organisations to store, process, and match specific quantities of biometric records—such as fingerprints, face images, and iris scans. These licences typically set hard caps on total database size (number of enrolled applicants) and concurrent system users. Since almost all government services are linked with national identity cards, the ABIS is an important component of the national identity card. The Department of Passports has been using the biometrics of the NID while preparing passports for service seekers.

“The price of the ABIS system will be finalised after the negotiation team concludes discussions and reaches an agreement,” Poudel said. “We have already communicated our decision to the company.”

According to the proposal, the government in March 2019 decided to expand the system’s capacity by procuring an additional 10 million ABIS licenses under the authority granted by a Cabinet decision dated March 25, 2019. The expansion was intended to enable the registration of up to 30 million citizens.

The department said the proposed cost for each ABIS licence is 0.0995 Euros, the same price offered by the supplier in 2019, and that the Rastriya Swatantra Party government is proceeding with procurement at that rate.

“Since the ABIS system licence has already expired, the Department of National Identity and Civil Registration has been facing operational difficulties,” said another official. “As service seekers have been repeatedly experiencing problems, the government decided to procure the system in a government-to-government arrangement.”

A month ago, a meeting of senior government officials, including the sitting chief secretary, decided to proceed with an immediate procurement of the ABIS system, according to an official.

The meeting was held to fulfil the requirements of Clause 3 of the Public Procurement Act and Article 41, which allow direct procurement under given circumstances.

The government first launched the National Identity Card (NID) programme as a pilot in Panchthar district and among employees working at Singha Durbar in 2009.

IDEMIA, the company that supplied the system, is also the same company that printed Nepal’s passports for nearly 16 years. IDEMIA had three divisions, one of which—Smart Identity—was sold to IN Groupe in 2025. The Department of National Identity and Civil Registration says it is preparing to purchase additional ABIS licences from IN Groupe because the division responsible for Nepal’s ABIS licences was transferred to the French company.

However, officials have not provided a clear justification for opting for direct procurement.

Article 41 of the Public Procurement Act allows direct procurement, among other conditions, when only one supplier has the technical capacity to meet procurement requirements; when only one supplier has exclusive rights to provide the goods and no suitable alternative is available; or when additional proprietary goods or services must be procured from an existing supplier to maintain compatibility with existing systems.

articles.title: From SLR rifles to DSLR cameras
articles.summary:
For 26 years, Sudeep KC trained his eyes on targets through the iron sights of an SLR rifle. Today, he uses the same discipline and precision to frame wildlife through the viewfinder of a camera.

The 58-year-old former Nepali Army colonel has spent the past seven years documenting Nepal’s birds, mammals and landscapes, transforming a military skill set built on patience, observation and accuracy into a career in wildlife photography.

His ability to locate elusive species, work in difficult terrain and capture wildlife in challenging conditions has earned him recognition among nature enthusiasts in Nepal and abroad. International photographers now travel to Nepal seeking his guidance on tracking wildlife and photographing species in their natural habitats.

A resident of Basundhara in Tokha Municipality-5, Kathmandu, KC retired from the army after a 26-year career and turned to wildlife photography full-time in 2019.

His interest in conservation began much earlier, during military postings to national parks where army units were deployed for security operations. Working alongside park officials, conservationists and nature guides introduced him to Nepal’s biodiversity and deepened his interest in wildlife.

Since taking up photography professionally, KC has photographed 595 bird species in Nepal.

“I have sighted more than 630 bird species in the wild,” KC told Kantipur. “But because of timing, weather conditions and physical limitations, I have not been able to photograph all of them.”

Nepal has officially recorded 903 bird species.

KC’s search for rare species has also taken him beyond Nepal. During photography expeditions to Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, he documented 378 bird species, many of which are not found in Nepal.

Among his most memorable achievements is photographing the Himalayan Monal, Nepal’s national bird.

“Capturing a clear image of the Monal required the greatest effort and persistence,” KC said. “I had been tracking the bird for a long time.”

He photographed the colourful pheasant at an altitude of 2,600 metres inside Shivapuri-Nagarjun National Park, and believes he was the first wildlife photographer to capture the species within the Kathmandu Valley.

“We had walked through dense forest for nearly four hours and were completely exhausted,” he recalled. “Just as we were about to turn back disappointed, the bird appeared right in front of us. Others with me also saw it, but I managed to frame and capture it first.”

From the Tarai plains to the Himalayas

KC spends three to four months every year travelling across Nepal in search of wildlife, moving from the grasslands of the Tarai to the high-altitude landscapes of the Himalayas.

When in Kathmandu, he regularly visits local wetlands, ridgelines and forest patches to photograph birds.

His portfolio includes grassland species, migratory winter and summer visitors, forest birds and farmland species. He has photographed the Spiny Babbler, believed to be Nepal’s only endemic bird species, as well as rare sightings such as the Mandarin Duck.

Beyond birds, KC has documented 25 species of mammals and reptiles, including the Royal Bengal tiger, sloth bear, leopard, one-horned rhinoceros, Asian elephant, spotted deer, barking deer, blackbuck, otter, Gangetic dolphin and Indian python.

Since beginning wildlife photography, he has encountered 12 wild tigers, successfully photographing most of them.

“I prefer photographing tigers in their natural habitat rather than taking close-up portraits,” he said. “Habitat photography requires patience, tracking skills and long hours in the field. The excitement of seeing a tiger in dense forest never disappears.”

He recalled following tiger footprints for four days inside Bardiya National Park before capturing an image of an adult tiger crossing a river at Tinkune, Bardiya.

But wildlife photography has also brought moments of danger.

“While on a full-day jungle walk with ornithologist Ram Shahi in Bardiya, a full-grown tiger appeared on the trail just three to four metres ahead of us,” KC said. “Adrenaline took over. Instead of raising the camera, our first instinct was to find safety.”

Two hours later, when they spotted the same tiger from a safer distance, KC said his hands were still shaking.

In another encounter in Sukebar, Chitwan, he had to climb a tree after unexpectedly coming across a one-horned rhinoceros.

Photographing the elusive Red Panda in the snow-covered forests of Nanggin Got inside Langtang National Park required waiting in freezing conditions for three consecutive days.

“Wildlife photography demands immense patience,” KC said. “Every second matters. You have to move quietly, understand animal behaviour and capture angles that make your work different.”

His assignments have taken him to more than 40 districts across Nepal, from the plains of the Tarai to Upper Dolpa.

Guiding international photographers

KC’s wildlife photographs shared on social media have attracted international photographers interested in Nepal’s biodiversity.

“Two months ago, a group of four Japanese photographers visited Nepal,” he said. “I guided them to key habitats where they successfully photographed several native bird and mammal species.”

Two years ago, KC was appointed Nepal Country Representative for the Asian Wildlife Photography Club (AWPC).

Through the organisation, he leads annual photography tours for visitors from Singapore, Malaysia, India and Sri Lanka to biodiversity hotspots including Chitwan, Bardiya and the Kathmandu Valley.

“When visiting photographers capture high-quality images here and display them abroad, it helps promote Nepal’s ecotourism,” KC said. “Nepal has rich wildlife resources that can attract nature enthusiasts from around the world.”

His photographs have been featured in calendars, brochures and books published by the National Trust for Nature Conservation, Bird Conservation Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board and international journals.

KC sees a strong connection between his military training and photography.

“In both disciplines, you aim with one eye, stabilise your body, hold your breath and act at the right moment without shaking,” he said. “In the army, we use camouflage and concealment so the target does not detect us. In wildlife photography, camouflage helps prevent disturbing animals.”

“Pulling the trigger of a rifle fires a bullet; pressing the shutter of a camera captures an image.”

From soldier to conservationist

KC’s photographs of landscapes, cultural heritage and rural life have won recognition in national competitions.

In 2025, he secured first place and a cash prize of Rs50,000 in the non-military category of a national photography competition organised by the Nepal Army. Three years earlier, he won second prize in a national contest organised by Kia Motors.

KC joined the Nepal Army as a Second Lieutenant in 1990, with his first posting at Chitwan National Park.

Working alongside park staff, conservationists and nature guides sparked his interest in wildlife tracking and species identification.

In 1991, he participated in the translocation of four one-horned rhinoceroses from Chitwan to Bardiya National Park.

“Before joining the military, I had a general interest in birdwatching,” he said. “My time in Chitwan deepened that interest. During long patrols, I carried binoculars and field guides to identify species along the trail.”

After two years in Chitwan, KC was transferred to Kathmandu, where he served for more than 12 years as a close protection officer for the royal family. During royal visits to Bardiya and Chitwan, he often informally guided visitors on wildlife.

Following the 2001 royal palace incident, KC was posted to Bardiya National Park as a major, commanding an army company responsible for park security during the Maoist conflict.

“Operating from national park barracks during the conflict brought different challenges,” he said. “We had to secure our positions, protect military assets and safeguard wildlife from poachers at the same time.”

During his military career, KC spent more than 14 years stationed in protected areas, including Shey-Phoksundo National Park, Rara National Park and Parsa Wildlife Reserve, now Parsa National Park.

While commanding forces in Bardiya, he led anti-poaching operations in coordination with park authorities.

In 2011-12, joint operations in the Surkhet-Barahatal buffer zone recovered 242 illegal muzzle-loading firearms.

Later, in 2015, during a military health camp in Upper Dolpa, his unit confiscated illegally stored snow leopard pelts based on local intelligence.

The photographer’s tools

KC began his photography journey with a Canon 6D Mark II paired with a 150-600mm zoom lens.

After consulting international wildlife photographers, he upgraded his equipment.

He now uses a Sony Alpha 1 camera body, valued at around Rs900,000, with a 100-400mm G Master zoom lens worth approximately Rs350,000.

The equipment, he says, allows him to capture fast-moving wildlife with improved autofocus tracking and high-speed shutter performance.

For KC, however, the most important tools remain the ones he developed long before he picked up a camera: patience, discipline and the ability to wait for the right moment.

articles.title: Should Nepal restrict minors’ access to social media?
articles.summary:
Governments across the globe have started to move away from soft guidelines towards hard legal bans on social media access for minors. This global policy shift is driven by mounting evidence of social media-driven mental health crises, addictive platform designs, and rising cybercrime. Australia recently enacted a nationwide ban for those under 16. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia and Malaysia have introduced regulations to block under-16s from social media platforms. From January 2027, France will implement a law banning children under 15 from social media. Under these new rules, every user in France will eventually need to verify their age to access platforms. The United Kingdom and the European Union are currently drafting and deliberating on legislation to protect children in the digital space.

The arguments for such strict regulations are primarily grounded in public health concerns. Social media platforms are designed to be addictive, using features like infinite scrolling and autoplaying feeds to maximise user engagement. Research shows that adolescent brains, still developing impulse control, often cannot self-regulate against these triggers. Excessive screen time is directly linked to rising rates of depression, anxiety and body image issues among teenagers. Beyond mental health, unrestricted access exposes minors to predators, grooming and extortion. Furthermore, late-night notifications and compulsive scrolling disrupt sleep patterns essential for physical development in minors.

Critics of these bans raise several concerns, often secondary to the safety of the minors. Some argue that blanket bans violate the rights of children to information and participation in public life. They claim that youth might lose vital online support networks if they are unable to access social media platforms. Enforcement also carries risks, as mandatory age verification might require users to share sensitive personal information through biometrics and government IDs, creating privacy vulnerabilities. Additionally, tech-savvy teenagers may use VPNs to bypass restrictions, potentially pushing them into even less-regulated and more dangerous online spaces.

In South Asia, the legal landscape is already shifting to meet these threats. India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, which classifies anyone under 18 as a child, requires verifiable parental consent and bans platforms from tracking or profiling minors. Pakistan and Bangladesh are also engaged in active policy debates regarding nationwide bans for those under 16. Meanwhile, Nepal remains behind the curve and currently has no statutory minimum age for social media access. The current legal framework focuses on content moderation rather than restricting access.

Nepal cannot afford to lag behind any longer. While other nations build digital shields, Nepal’s youth remain exposed. Meanwhile, cybercrime against minors in the country has quadrupled in just three years. The rise of generative AI has worsened the situation, with deepfakes becoming common tools for peer harassment. The human cost in Nepal is already significant. One in three Nepali children has expressed a willingness to meet online ‘friends’ in person. Of those who do, nearly 28 percent encounter abusive behaviour. Nearly 40 percent of girls have received unsolicited explicit messages or images online. Mental health is suffering, with over 34 percent of teenagers spending up to six hours a day on social media. This leads to anxiety and academic decline.

Nepal must start an active and urgent discourse on social media regulation for minors. The country’s youth are navigating a digital minefield without adequate protection or literacy. The rise in online-to-offline predatory behaviour and AI-driven manipulation demands a stronger response than mere content moderation. Policymakers need to examine the models used across the world and draft one suitable for Nepal. Waiting for the problem to solve itself is not an option when the well-being of an entire generation is at stake. It is time for Nepal to build a legal framework that ensures child safety on social media platforms.

articles.title: How Modi’s BJP has lost its biggest edge
articles.summary:
The chain of events that have rocked India’s national capital, and indeed the entire nation, show that the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has lost its biggest edge—its ability to swiftly read the ground mood and tailor a reaction to it. The outrage on the streets of New Delhi that seems to be spilling over to other parts of the country is a clear reflection of how the BJP—once supremely astute, pragmatic and connected to the ground—now seems to be losing its touch, with hubris and complacency overtaking all else. The party is so drunk on years of power and popularity that it seems to think it is invincible and fully insulated from any public ire.

What started off as relatively low-key youth protests led by an online satire platform, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over the NEET paper leak (a highly competitive nationwide exam for those seeking admission to medical colleges), quickly snowballed into a national headline with activist Sonam Wangchuk joining the cause with an indefinite hunger strike. The situation was further aggravated when Wangchuk was forcibly removed by the government from the protest site and shifted to a hospital.

Things reached a crescendo when a Chalo Sansad protest announced for July 20 witnessed massive crowds running into several thousand—far, far more than anybody had anticipated—and the state reacted with a brutal police crackdown on youth protestors. The image of the police ruthlessly resorting to lathi charge, tear gas shelling and violence against protesting students shook a large section of the country. Visuals of the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi being dragged away unceremoniously by the police while protesting the next day only made matters worse.

The Modi government, however, continued to react with brazenness, refusing to sack Pradhan or to accept real responsibility for all that had transpired. Essentially, the BJP allowed the narrative to slip out of its control, a rare misstep by a party that has since 2014 mastered the art of perception management.

BJP track record

The BJP under PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah has been an election-winning juggernaut, a feat achieved through a bouquet of carefully crafted strategies, a key one being its ability to promptly and accurately read sentiment on the ground and react to it with alacrity and shrewdness.

For example, soon after it first came to power nationally in 2014, the BJP government attempted to dilute the Land Acquisition legislation (which essentially defines how the government can acquire private land for public projects while legally mandating fair compensation) to make it more industry-friendly and less tilted towards farmers and rural landowners. The move, which the government attempted to bulldoze through, invited much criticism from the rural poor, with the Congress campaign of suit boot ki sarkar (a government of the rich) gathering much traction. With its ear to the ground and realising the extent of resistance and resentment against the move, and the danger of being labelled as a ‘pro-rich’ regime, the Modi administration withdrew the decision and quickly dropped it as if it were a hot potato.

No ego. No false sense of complacency. No hubris.

This served it well, with the pivot quickly establishing it as a government of all sections, especially of the poor, and taking the winds out of the Congress campaign’s sails. The BJP has since gone on to win election after election, while the Congress has been in free fall.

The government similarly backtracked on the issue of new contentious farm laws in 2021 after a massive and sustained protest mounted by farmers threatened to damage its image and electoral fortunes. To be sure, the backtracking in this case took much longer, but eventually, it did happen.

Essentially, these examples show how this government has in the past displayed the ability to read the room and tweak its approach in response to public sentiment of a certain scale.

That, however, no longer seems to be the case. Buoyed by 12 years of election wins, including its ability to unseat difficult opponents, Modi’s BJP seems to be drowning in hubris and smugness. Unbridled power hasn’t spared the ruthlessly ambitious and astutely pragmatic Modi-Shah duo either, resulting in a situation where conceit seems to be getting the better of it.

Losing its touch

PM Modi has been a widely and wildly popular leader, and under him, the BJP has seen a sharp rise to near-absolute dominance. But the party and its leaders would do well to remember that it now has 12 years of incumbency behind it, which invariably brings with it some public fatigue, disillusionment, questions and even anger. No political player is insulated from these, not even this BJP.

The current mood among the nation’s youth should greatly worry the party. It has allowed things to escalate purely because its ego and arrogance overtook not just a sense of right and wrong, but also sheer practicality. All it needed to do initially was get the education minister to resign and own accountability for the rot in the education sector. For decades, ministers in the country have resigned over lapses in their sectors, most notably railways ministers after accidents and tragedies.

Modi-Shah, however, thought they could brazen it out and perhaps did not anticipate the scale of youth discomfort. What is happening today is nothing short of an uprising. Neighbouring Nepal’s example should tell the BJP how the youth can be a powerful harbinger of change. The state’s unforgivable violence against protesting youngsters is an image the nation is unlikely to forget or forgive soon. By allowing the matter to balloon to such an extent, the BJP has now boxed itself into a corner since any climbdown would now seem like a war lost to its opponents. And anything else other than full compliance with the demands of protestors will just seem like a cop-out and a case of very little, very late, including the PM’s attempts at outreach.

The youth is genuinely angry. The youth is disenchanted. The youth is seeking accountability. Modi’s BJP would do well not to continue dismissing these protests as manufactured anger or an orchestrated movement. The youth has been among BJP’s most crucial vote bank, lapping up its promise of vikas. But the younger generation that stood by Modi in 2014 and 2019 is no longer young. The youth today is a very new generation that perhaps has barely voted before and on whose mind the image of an unaccountable, intolerant BJP behaving like a tyrant is being imprinted.

PM Modi’s BJP has pushed it too far this time. This is not just a youth movement. This is an uprising.

articles.title: All is not well with the RSP
articles.summary:
A little over half of the electorate did not vote for the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) in the general elections a few months ago. As one of that multitude, I guess I have some right to speak for them. For I am sure I am not alone in facing the paradox of looking askance at a government led by someone one had fervently hoped would not prevail while also equally fervently hoping that the said individual and his team succeed.

Such has been the collective dilemma for many since Balendra Shah assumed charge as prime minister, leading a parliamentary majority that most politicians can only dream of. As a Cabinet of relative youngsters took over the government, there was expectedly a measure of optimism among RSP voters (and others as well) that the country would now finally shift gears. Unfortunately, four months later, the initial doubts about the RSP are coming to light.

The positive aspect of having newcomers hold the reins is that they would still be driven by idealism and open to innovative approaches, enabling a fresh start. The flip side to that would always be that their collective inexperience and lack of understanding of the political exigencies required to balance the different interest groups would become apparent. Expectedly, the government has taken one misstep after another with the arrest and court-ordered release of former prime minister KP Sharma Oli and others, and the inhumane haste with which the squatter settlements were demolished being two early examples.

Of ambassadors and envoys

The wholesale recall of all politically appointed ambassadors from around the world and its aftermath is another instance of not having thought things through. The practice until now that half the ambassadors would be foreign service cadre and half appointed at will by the ruling party(ies) was not conducive to the conduct of much meaningful diplomacy in the case of the latter. Particularly when they were recalled with every change of government in Kathmandu. The solution, the RSP believes, is to select ambassadorships through open competition. Accordingly, the government is now engaged in a mammoth exercise of sifting through the 4,500 or so applications it has received in response to its call.

To begin with, I fail to understand why people place such a premium on becoming an ambassador. Apart from serving the Nepali diaspora spread across the globe, there is little diplomacy to engage in since we are too unimportant to merit any attention. I think the only place where Nepali diplomats are accorded any respect is Lhasa, although all we have there is a consul general, heading the only foreign mission there. Everywhere else, even in India and China, we really do not matter. A headline published in this daily in 2023 says it all: ‘Nepal’s ambassadors wait—months on end—for political access in Delhi, Beijing.’

Secondly, if the whole point of sending an ambassador is to further a country’s interests, selecting someone through open competition can hardly be the best way to go about it. It may seem like a fair approach, but unlike other public sector jobs, an ambassador must be totally in tune with their government back home, and that is not necessarily what someone chosen via a selection process is likely to be. Why the RSP insists on filling half the ambassadorial positions from outside the foreign ministry is still a mystery. Career diplomats are usually best placed to serve as ambassadors, although outsiders might have to be brought in depending on circumstances.

Take the case of how India does things. A few months ago, amid deteriorating relations with Bangladesh, the government sent a senior leader of the ruling party as its top envoy to Dhaka. Such an individual with direct access to the highest echelons of power back home can be instrumental in repairing strained ties. (For the record, there is currently only one other political appointee among the more than 200 ambassadors and consul generals India has around the world.)

The utility of such an appointment became clear even in Nepal back in 1989–90 when we had suffered through an Indian blockade. As soon as a new government took over, New Delhi first sent SK Sinha, the dhaka topi-wearing, Nepali-speaking, retired general with a background in a Gorkha regiment. Sinha was followed by another well-wisher of Nepal, Bimal Prasad, an academic who was known personally to many Nepali leaders. The goodwill generated by these two genuine friends of Nepal at such a difficult time in Nepal-India ties cannot be underestimated.
